explanation: The Romans called it Quintilis, the fifth month, because their year once began in March. It was renamed in Caesar's honour in 44 BC, the year of his death, and August later honoured Augustus.

evidence.query: Roman calendar year originally began in March Quintilis Sextilis renamed August after Augustus
evidence.summaryExcerpt: Original March start: Historians infer that the year began in March, because the months after June are numbered rather than named. The Romans did not have records of their early calendars but, like modern historians, assumed the year originally began in March on the basis of the names of the months following June. Ten-month calendar: The Romans traced their first calendar to Romulus, with ten months, beginning in spring with March and leaving winter as an unassigned span of days before the next year.
